### What a TPD Lawyer Does

- **Checks your coverage:** Many people do not realize they have TPD insurance bundled into their superannuation accounts. A lawyer can search for multiple policies across different funds.
- **Gathers evidence:** They collect medical records, employment histories, and expert reports required to match strict policy definitions.
- **Handles denials:** Insurers routinely reject initial claims. A specialist lawyer can appeal the decision and negotiate a fair settlement.[[1]](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/supertalk-blog/2026/january/common-challenges-tpd-claims/)[[2]](https://comparepersonalinjurylawyers.com.au/tpd-lawyer-unley/)[[3]](https://www.fiftyplussa.com.au/lifestyle/life/arentz-advises-understand-total-permanent-disability-claims/)[[4]](https://www.mkflawyers.com.au/post/what-injuries-or-illnesses-can-i-claim-tpd-insurance-for)

### Costs and Timeframes

- **No Win, No Fee:** Most TPD lawyers operate on a conditional fee structure, meaning you pay legal costs only if your claim succeeds.
- **Average Payout:** Payouts typically range from $60,000 to $600,000 depending on your policy terms.
- **Timeframe:** Claims generally take between 12 to 18 months to resolve.[[1]](https://www.fiftyplussa.com.au/lifestyle/life/arentz-advises-understand-total-permanent-disability-claims/)[[2]](https://splattlawyers.com.au/tpd-payout-calculator/)
